I have a big server just like you do. It's one of the older big IBM Xservers, with Dual power supplies, Dual SCSI Disk Controllers with fail over, and what I do with it is use the Wake on land feature. I set up a backup schedule controller on a $79.00 Zotac ZBOXNANO-VD01-U that uses a flash drive as it's storage media. This thing runs all the time. How this works is the Zotac is the back up controller. At 2:30 AM it wakes up the desk tops, (Mine, My Wife's, and our kids) and the Server via wake on lan. When the client machines have booted the Zotac tells them it's time to start the back up. The server auto loads the back up program at boot time. The server checks the time and if it is between 2:30 and 3:00 AM the Server attaches to the client drives that are to be backed up and starts spinning data. When the backup is finished the back up log files are created, stored and the Server powers its self down. When the desk tops have finished backing up they power down. This is a no mus and no fuss way to back up. I also might add that the Server checks the creation date and time of the file, if it hasn't changed from the previous nights log file entry then the file is skipped and not backed up, how ever the file name is annotated why it was not backed up in the back up log file. (The annotation contains the last date and time the file was last backed up.) The whole thing works pretty slick. By the way my IBM Xserver is running Ubuntu sever 15.10 (I think) Also I might ad that the Server has 6, 300GB Ultra320 SCSI Drives and the IBM EXP400 expansion chassis has space for another 14 300GB Ultra320 SCSI drives for a total drive space of 20 300GB SCSI Drives. ( I am running only 10 Drives a the current time. You know money is still a limiting factor) 300GB ultra320 SCSI Drives cost about 35 a hit. I run 1.5 TB of RAID 5 for the backup and 600GB of RAID 10 for the log files and other system related stuff.
